selected_result: Theorem 3.5: probabilistic componentwise backward error for triangular substitution

bibliographic_source.title: A New Approach to Probabilistic Rounding Error Analysis

task_clarification: Let T in R^(n x n) be nonsingular triangular and solve T*x=b by floating-point substitution under Model 2.1, obtaining xHat.
For every lambda>0, with probability at least Q(lambda,n*(n+1)/2), there exists DeltaT with (T+DeltaT)*xHat=b and |DeltaT|<=gammaTilde_n(lambda)*|T| componentwise.
The source proves the lower-triangular orientation without loss of generality; the theorem does not restrict the input to that branch.
scope_constraints: Retain nonsingularity, triangularity, both source-allowed orientations, and the exact probability and perturbation coefficients.
The output xHat must come from the modeled substitution algorithm; it cannot be an arbitrary vector satisfying the conclusion by assumption.
Do not assume the final perturbation or event as a field of the run.
